_environment: torch 2.15.0 (pip wheel, Python 3.12.11, throwaway uv venv at a throwaway uv venv outside the repo; repo .venv untouched). macOS 27.0.1 build 26A434, arm64 M1 Max (same host as findings.md). Run GPU-serialized via bench/with_gpu.sh; exit 0. Method: 2 warmup calls per variant, then 5 rounds x 3 timed calls per variant, variants interleaved round-robin within each round, torch.mps.synchronize after every call, median and IQR over the 15 samples; timing structure copied from bench/bench_int8_linear.py:14-19 (warmup, repeats, sync, median). _int_mm variant: int8 x [M,K] @ contiguous int8 w.t() [K,N] -> int32, no scale restore; dequant-per-call variant: (int8 w).to(fp16) * per-row fp16 scale then F.linear. Correctness check: torch._int_mm on MPS vs int64 CPU matmul at (256,1024,512) and (4608,16384,6144), max abs diff 0 at both. Caveats: single process, one host state snapshot not recorded (no pmset/powermetrics), 15 samples per cell; the review's should-fix variance protocol (3+ fresh processes, bootstrap CI) was not applied in this cheap version. No repo files were edited in this task, so there are no file:line changes to report.
_interpretation: torch 2.15.0 does ship a working MPS torch._int_mm on this M1 Max (macOS 27.0.1): it did not raise NotImplementedError and its int32 output is bit-exact against an int64 CPU reference, so findings.md:24 ("not implemented on MPS in torch 2.14.1") needs the "torch <= 2.14" qualifier the review's M8 asks for. At the two K=6144 shapes _int_mm is not faster than fp16 F.linear: 42.1 vs 39.4 ms (1.07x slower) and 113.4 vs 104.5 ms (1.08x slower), and it lands within noise of the repo's weight-only Metal kernel at the same shapes (39.5 and 104.7 ms, findings.md:78-79) while still omitting the per-call scale restore that a real INT8 linear needs. At K=16384 _int_mm (112.6 ms) is 2.0x faster than fp16 F.linear (226.3 ms), but that is the same wide-K F.linear anomaly already logged at findings.md:25; against the bare fp16 GEMM (103 ms, findings.md:80) and the repo kernel (107 ms) it is about 5-9% slower, so the "2x" is a statement about F.linear's slow path, not about integer compute, matching the M4 correction the review applies to the repo's own K=16384 claim.
